options.text: Acts perpendicular to the direction of motion
Always speeds objects up
Opposes the motion or attempted motion between two surfaces
Only acts on stationary objects

questions.explanation: Friction is a resistive force that opposes the sliding or attempted sliding of two surfaces in contact.

questions.stem: In which medium does drag act on a moving object?

options.text: Only in solids
Only in water
Only in a vacuum
In fluids (liquids and gases)

questions.explanation: Drag acts on objects moving through fluids, which include both liquids and gases (including air resistance).

questions.stem: What happens to air resistance as the speed of a falling object increases?

options.text: It increases
It stays the same
It decreases
It becomes zero

questions.explanation: Air resistance (drag) increases as speed increases. The faster an object moves through air, the greater the drag force acting on it.

options.text: Drag force equals the weight of the object, so acceleration is zero
All forces on the object are removed
The object begins to slow down
The object reaches its maximum possible speed

questions.explanation: Terminal velocity occurs when drag equals weight, making the resultant force zero. The object then falls at a constant velocity with no further acceleration.

questions.stem: Which factor does NOT affect the friction between two surfaces?

options.text: The roughness of the surfaces
The normal force pressing them together
The materials the surfaces are made from
The colour of the surfaces

questions.explanation: Friction depends on the nature of the surfaces (roughness and material) and the normal force, but not on the colour of the surfaces.

questions.stem: Why is rolling friction less than sliding friction?

options.text: Because rolling objects move slower
Because rolling friction acts upward
Because rolling involves less surface contact and deformation than sliding
Because rolling objects are always lighter

questions.explanation: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction because there is less deformation and surface contact. This is why wheels are used for transport.

questions.stem: A skydiver has just jumped from a plane and is accelerating downward. Which statement is correct?

options.text: There is no air resistance yet
Air resistance is greater than weight
Weight and air resistance are equal
Weight is greater than air resistance

questions.explanation: While the skydiver is accelerating downward, weight must be greater than air resistance, creating a net downward force. As speed increases, drag increases until terminal velocity is reached.
